annotations.description: Burnout Bashtronaut has speed 2 and is progressing toward max speed (double strike), but it's only a 1/1 that costs R to replay. Hired Claw is a 1/2 that deals 1 damage whenever Lizards attack (essentially free damage each turn) and can grow with +1/+1 counters. However, the Bashtronaut's speed mechanic is persistent and doesn't reset when replayed - it will come back at the same speed level and continue scaling toward double strike, making it increasingly dangerous. That said, Hired Claw provides consistent value and is harder to deal with at 1/2 (survives more removal). The decision is close but bouncing Hired Claw may have been slightly better since it provides guaranteed damage each attack step and can grow, while Bashtronaut at speed 2 is still just a 1/1 menace for now and the opponent needs to spend mana on its pump ability to make it threatening.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Burnout Bashtronaut instead of Hired Claw
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Hired Claw, which provides free damage on every Lizard attack and can permanently grow with +1/+1 counters, representing more consistent long-term value for the opponent

annotations.description: GLM47 Vorthos warped Nova Hellkite for {2}{R} instead of first playing the Mountain from hand (giving 5 lands total) and hardcasting it for {3}{R}{R}. The Warp version will be exiled at end of turn, losing a permanent 4/5 flying haste threat on the board. Playing the land first would allow the full cast, keeping the dragon permanently.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite with Warp for {2}{R} without playing land first, meaning it will be exiled at end of turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain first (5th land), then hardcast Nova Hellkite for {3}{R}{R} to keep it permanently on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Casting Nova Hellkite for its Warp cost ({2}{R}) from exile means it gets exiled at end of turn, losing a powerful 4/5 flying body permanently. The opponent is a blue-based deck with limited shown removal, so a permanent 4/5 flyer would be very difficult to deal with and represents recurring damage every turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite from exile for Warp cost ({2}{R}), getting one attack but losing the creature at end step.
annotations.betterLine: Hard cast Nova Hellkite from hand for {3}{R}{R} (5 mana available), keeping the 4/5 flying haste permanently on board. While this uses all mana, the permanent threat is worth significantly more than deploying a small additional creature alongside a temporary dragon.

annotations.description: Targeted Tiger-Seal (3/3) with Nova Hellkite's 1 damage ETB trigger, leaving it alive at 3/2. The Otter Token (1/1 with prowess) would have been killed outright by the 1 damage, actually removing a threat from the board. Dealing 1 damage to a 3/3 is largely inconsequential as it doesn't change relevant combat math.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Tiger-Seal with Nova Hellkite's 1 damage, leaving it alive as a 3/2
annotations.betterLine: Target the Otter Token to kill it outright, removing a creature from the board and clearing blockers for attacks

annotations.description: Nova Hellkite is a 4/5 flying haste creature threatening 4 damage per turn, and the opponent is tapped out with all 4 Mountains tapped. Bouncing Nova Hellkite would remove the biggest threat on the board and force the opponent to re-spend 5 mana (or 3 for Warp) to replay it. Instead, bouncing Tiger-Seal to draw a card is extremely low-value — Tiger-Seal enters tapped on upkeep anyway and is a defensive creature that doesn't address the opponent's board pressure. The card draw from bouncing Tiger-Seal doesn't compensate for leaving a 4/5 flyer on the board that will continue attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced own Tiger-Seal with Boomerang Basics to draw a card
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Nova Hellkite with Boomerang Basics to remove the opponent's most dangerous threat while they're tapped out, forcing them to re-cast it next turn

annotations.description: Casting Lightning Strike during precombat main phase is a sequencing error. If targeting the opponent's face, it should be saved for after combat or end of opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility. If targeting the 1/1 Otter Token, it's an inefficient use of a 3-damage burn spell on a 1/1 creature when the main damage dealer (Nova Hellkite) has flying and doesn't need the path cleared.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Strike during precombat main phase instead of attacking first
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Nova Hellkite and Hired Claw first, then cast Lightning Strike after combat or hold it for later turns when it could represent lethal or answer a real threat

annotations.description: Tiger-Seal is a ground creature that cannot block Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying), which is the primary threat at 12 life. The player should have addressed the flying threat first. Additionally, casting a spell before playing a land drop is a minor sequencing error.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tiger-Seal, a 3/3 ground creature that can't block the Nova Hellkite flying threat.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island/Spirebluff Canal first (land drop), then either cast Quantum Riddler for Warp {1}{U} to get a 4/6 flying blocker that draws a card and can block/trade with Nova Hellkite, or cast Boomerang Basics targeting Nova Hellkite to bounce it while opponent's Mountains are tapped and they can't recast it this turn.

annotations.description: The reasoning explicitly states blocking Nova Hellkite with Tiger-Seal, but Nova Hellkite has flying and Tiger-Seal cannot block it. The game system likely assigned Tiger-Seal to block a Hired Claw instead. Additionally, not also blocking with Otter Token on the second Hired Claw means taking 1 extra damage (going from 10 to potentially 5 instead of 6 after the unblockable Hellkite hits). At 10 life against an aggressive red deck, every point matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Tiger-Seal as sole blocker (likely assigned to a Hired Claw), letting the other Hired Claw and Nova Hellkite through for 6 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block with both Tiger-Seal and Otter Token on the two Hired Claws to minimize damage taken, only letting the unblockable Nova Hellkite through for 4 damage instead of 5-6.

annotations.description: Casting Lightning Strike before combat when lethal damage is already available on board through attacking. Nova Hellkite (4 flying) + Sunspine Lynx (5) + Hired Claw (1 + 1 trigger) = 11 damage against opponent at 6 life with only a tapped blocker. Spending the Lightning Strike pre-combat wastes a card and removes backup burn if combat goes wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lightning Strike (presumably targeting opponent) before combat when lethal was available on board
annotations.betterLine: Go directly to combat and attack with all creatures for lethal, keeping Lightning Strike in hand as insurance against any combat tricks or removal
